title: Peach and almond loaf cake
subtitle: a moist almond loaf cake with fresh peach pieces folded through and an almond crust on top
excerpt: Peach and almond loaf cake is a moist, dense loaf built around ground almonds and sliced fresh peaches folded through the batter. The ground almonds make the crumb richer and heavier than a flour-only cake, and the peach softens into the batter as it bakes. A scatter of flaked almonds on top gives a crunchy contrast to the soft crumb below.
sourceNotes: Almond and stone-fruit combinations are common in French and Italian baking, particularly in the Piedmont and Provence regions where both almonds and stone fruits are cultivated. The loaf cake format reflects British home baking tradition; the combination became popular in the UK through the influence of writers including Nigel Slater.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice before freezing. Wrap individually and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for 3 to 4 days. Better the day after baking.

content.text: Peach and almond loaf cake is a dense, moist loaf made with ground almonds alongside the flour. The ground almonds add richness, a slightly damp crumb, and a gentle almond flavour that works well with the fresh peach pieces folded through the batter. The peach softens as it bakes, so the crumb is fragrant and fruity rather than identifiably chunky. It keeps well.

items.prepNote: peeled, stoned, cut into 1 cm pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to 170 degrees C (fan 150 degrees C / gas 3 to 4). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the almond extract.
Fold in the flour, ground almonds, and baking powder until just combined. Fold in the peach pieces gently. The batter will be thick.
Spoon into the prepared tin and smooth the top. Scatter the flaked almonds over the surface.

Bake for 50 to 55 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean and the top is golden. If the almonds on top are browning too fast, cover loosely with foil after 35 minutes. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.

attrs.problem: Cake sinking in the middle after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid opening the oven door in the first 40 minutes; the temperature drop causes the centre to sink before it can set.
attrs.fix: Wait until at least 45 minutes before checking. If the cake is sinking consistently, the oven temperature may be too high. Use an oven thermometer to check.

attrs.problem: Peach pieces making the base of the cake wet
attrs.avoid: Avoid very ripe or juicy peaches that break down during baking and release too much liquid.
attrs.fix: Pat the peach pieces dry before folding in. Using slightly under-ripe peaches works better in baked goods as they hold their shape and release less juice.
